searches.note: Twenty four searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, four left unspent for the run's shared allowance. The shared search went to the law of the DOC (Portaria 140/2010 of 5 March, read through a Diário da República mirror and the CVR Tejo's own page, with Decreto-Lei 45/2000 for the Ribatejo's statutes). One search was restricted to a house's own domain (alorna.pt, read as primary through its summary) and one to the house and four Portuguese wine magazines; every other search blocked the author's sources (the house itself where the account had to be independent, Wikipedia, Infopedia, Continente, Firstleaf, Tanners, the CVR Tejo, Visit Lisboa, Cave Lusa, Vinoscout, Wine House Portugal, the MG club and Enotur). Writers' own sites that came up were read and never cited. No fetch tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the law and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the dates the stories turn on (the founder of Alorna and his titles, 1723 and 1918, 1775, 1648 and 1926, 1834 and the Palmela marriage, 1836, 1881 and 1975), then to the making of each flagship against sheets the author had not read, then to the others and the places.

Where the house's own page met an independent account that contradicted it, the house's fact was cut or narrowed (the dovecote's century, the marriage of 1846); where figures differed by vintage they were widened and tied to the vintage (Falcoaria's oak, the 1836's oak); where a fact rested on one listing it was taken out (Terra de Lobos, the Reserva's DOC, a varietal Merlot).

tested: The founder and his titles, the author's Infopedia and Wikipedia blocked: Pedro Miguel de Almeida Portugal, third Count of Assumar, 1688 to 1756 (Portugal, Dicionário Histórico at arqnet, Geni, Geneall: the days differ, the years agree); viceroy of India from 1744 (the FCSH NOVA list gives 1744 to 1750, with the titles Marquis of Castelo Novo and Marquis of Alorna); the fortress of Alorna taken in 1746 and the title redesignated in 1748 by a royal letter of 9 November (Grokipedia, arqnet). Borne out. One magazine says the title came from King José I, which is wrong for 1748, so the record keeps the king.

The estate's dates, the house blocked: 1723, the first name Quinta de Vale de Nabais, the renaming after Alorna, the sale by the poet's daughters to the Counts of Junqueira and the public auction (Revista de Vinhos, Clube de Vinhos Portugueses, Rota dos Vinhos do Tejo); 1918 and the five generations (the state heritage inventory SIPA on monumentos.gov.pt, which names the house Palácio dos Marqueses de Alorna, Casa da Quinta de Vale de Nabais, and Portugal by Wine). Borne out, save the heirs' auction.

The poet and the range: the house's Undiscovered wines page names its Marquesa de Alorna wine a tribute to Leonor de Almeida Portugal (1750 to 1839), the fourth Marquise, a pre-Romantic poet, and Revista de Vinhos says the Grande Reserva white honours the fourth Marquise, the poet Alcipe. Borne out.

The making: fourteen months in new French oak and about twelve months in bottle on Diwines, Garrafeira 5 Estrelas and others (one 2019 listing gives twelve months in oak); the blend secret on two listings; the house's own sheet on its domain gives fourteen months, grapes from the Lezíria and the Charneca on sandy clays and sandy loams, floral and black fruit over cedar, and 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; its bottle time reads twelve months on one page and two years on another.

The others: 1723 is a Grande Reserva red made for the tricentenary in a limited edition (the house's shop, Diário de Notícias, Clube de Vinhos Portugueses); the Reserva Touriga Nacional and Cabernet Sauvignon is DOC do Tejo from the Charneca only, by the house's own sheets for the 2020 and the 2022.

The questions: one right answer each, options of one kind (four oak regimes, four deeds); the Brazil distractor names a real post of the founder, so the explanation now says so and why it is wrong. The house rules: nobody living named, no price (the 1723's price met and not used), no score, nothing volatile (the 2019's bottle count met and not used), no judging superlative, British, no dash.

tested: The house's story, the house and the CVR Tejo blocked: 1775 and the family ever since (Grandes Escolhas, Revista de Vinhos and others; one account gives 1755); a royal hunting ground for four centuries (two accounts; one puts its end in the late eighteenth century); the royal falcon hunts and the range named for them (Grandes Escolhas). Borne out. The dovecote: one account calls it centuries old and used to train the falcons, another dates the surviving tower to the nineteenth century, and none but the house gives the sixteenth.

The making, the house, the CVR Tejo and Tanners blocked: Castelão, Alicante Bouschet, Touriga Nacional and Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot in some listings; cement tanks with temperature control; part of the oldest vines trodden in cement lagares in exceptional years on one sheet; twelve months in French oak, half new and half of second or third use, on the 2021 sheet at Casa do Vinho de Almeirim and on Wineclick, against the author's thirteen on the CVR Tejo's sheet.

The law, the IVV blocked: Portaria 140/2010 of 5 March recognised the DO do Tejo in place of Ribatejo (a Diário da República mirror and the CVR Tejo's DOC page); Decreto-Lei 45/2000 of 21 March approved the Ribatejo region's statutes; the regional wine's name changed in 2009 (Portaria 445/2009 by DFJ Vinhos and Wine Searcher).

The others: the Falcoaria Vinhas Velhas white is Fernão Pires of old vines (Wineclick, Grandes Escolhas); the Colheita Tardia comes in half bottles (The Wine Jungle, Wineexpert); Terra de Lobos was not found.

The questions: one right answer each; a lagar distractor was too near the truth for some vintages and was replaced. The house rules: the family and its winemakers never named; no price (met and not used), no award, nothing volatile (hectares met and not used), British, no dash.

tested: The estate's history, the house and Wikipedia blocked: the palace tied to Queen Leonor of Austria until 1530, when she married Francis I of France (Público's Fugas); the Counts of Odemira, Maria de Faro's marriage to the first Duke of Cadaval and the dukedom of 1648 (Fugas, e-cultura, Clube de Vinhos Portugueses); the stud founded in 1648; five generations of women. Borne out, the queen's dwelling narrowed.

The marquise, Visit Lisboa, Time Out and the house blocked: Olga Maria Nicolis di Robilant, born in Turin on 17 January 1900, married in Venice in July 1926 to António Caetano Álvares Pereira de Melo, Marquis of Cadaval (1894 to 1939), settled at the Quinta da Piedade, Colares, in 1929, died in Lisbon on 21 December 1996 and buried in the family mausoleum at Muge (the Portuguese Wikipedia, Geneall, Geni, the Centro Cultural Olga Cadaval, the Almeirim library's page). Borne out, and her dates now let her be named.

The flagship, Cave Lusa and Continente blocked: Touriga Nacional, Trincadeira and Alicante Bouschet, each fermented apart in stainless steel at 26 degrees, about three weeks' maceration, the malolactic in new French oak, sixteen months there and twelve in bottle (the house's sheet, Gota a Gota, Degostar); the vines fifty years old on the house's sheet and twenty on Gota a Gota. Whether the wine was named for the marquise was not found.

The others: the Reserva is Touriga Nacional, Trincadeira, Alicante Bouschet and Alfrocheiro, with Merlot in the 2020 (granvine, Tesouros de Baco); varietal Cabernet Sauvignon and Pinot Noir listed, a varietal Trincadeira only on a blog of 2006 and the author's listing, no varietal Merlot found.

The questions: one right answer each, four blends and four years; the wine question's explanation claimed a varietal Merlot and was rewritten. The house rules: the woman who has chaired the house since 1998 is not named; no score (met and not used), no price, nothing volatile (the estate's hectares and bottle counts met and not used), British, no dash.

tested: The estate's history, the house and the CVR Tejo blocked: bought in 1834 by Henrique Teixeira de Sampaio, first Count of Póvoa, after the orders' lands were sold (Grandes Escolhas, Clube de Vinhos Portugueses); the property passed to the heiress Maria Luísa de Noronha e Sampaio in 1841 to 1842 and to the house of Palmela in 1842 (Enotur, a magazine); the marriage given as 1846 by the MG club page and Enotur, which follow the house.

The marriage, the house, the MG club and Enotur blocked: Geni gives 3 July 1836 for the marriage of Domingos de Sousa Holstein (1818 to 1864), later second Duke of Palmela, to Luísa Maria de Noronha e Sampaio, daughter of the Count of Póvoa; the Capet genealogy gives the same, or France 1840; a betrothal deed of 6 September 1834 is reported; their daughter, later third Duchess of Palmela, was born in 1841. The house's 1846 does not stand against a daughter born in 1841, and the marriage year is left out.

The flagship, Vinoscout, Wine House Portugal and Continente blocked: the Grande Escolha Alfrocheiro made only in exceptional years, its malolactic in new and one year old French oak and ten to twelve months there (VelvetBull, Garrafeira 5 Estrelas); Grandes Escolhas calls it the estate's flagship, the 2016 the last of fifteen editions, from a lagar with mechanical treading and new and used French oak; the name since moved to Grande Reserva, with an organic bottling (Viva o Vinho). The house's making page belongs to that later bottling.

The others: Dona Isabel Juliana is a Grande Reserva white and red and a Grande Reserva Bruto sparkling wine the trade press calls the top of the range (Viva o Vinho, Hipersuper, Gazeta Rural, Garrafinhas); the Reserva Alfrocheiro and Syrah is borne out by Hipersuper.

The questions: one right answer each; the story question no longer rests on 1846. The house rules: the family that holds the estate is not named; no price (met and not used), no score, nothing volatile (bottle counts met and not used), British, no dash.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment's prose, titles or addresses. The dead met are named only where two sources give their dates: Olga Nicolis di Robilant (1900 to 1996) is now named in the Cadaval story; Pedro Miguel de Almeida Portugal (1688 to 1756) and Leonor de Almeida Portugal (1750 to 1839) stand as the author named them. Manuel Caroça (1872 to 1945, by SIPA), the Marquis of Cadaval (1894 to 1939), Domingos de Sousa Holstein (1818 to 1864), the first Count of Póvoa and his daughter are dead and are described, not named, their dates in one source or none. The refuter did not edit people.json; the read together agent adds those it judges living.
swapNote: The author proposed no swap, and the refuter proposes none. The author's suggestion that the plan's wine for quinta-da-lagoalva be renamed Grande Reserva Alfrocheiro is refused: the Grande Escolha Alfrocheiro is the label a guest meets on bottles to the 2016, in fifteen editions by Grandes Escolhas, which calls it the estate's flagship, and the record already teaches the later Grande Reserva name in its label and its story. The read together agent may weigh the Dona Isabel Juliana Grande Reserva red, which trade press calls the house's top red, first made in 2009, if it judges the pick should follow the house's present range. The other four picks stand: each is a real house of the Tejo with the wine it leads with (the Marquesa de Alorna Grande Reserva red, Falcoaria Tinto, the Marquesa de Cadaval red, the 1836 Grande Reserva red).
planNotes: quinta-da-alorna: answered. 1723 and the marquisate of 1748 after Alorna in 1746 are borne out; the red is taught, its grapes the house's secret; the white is in others.

casal-branco: answered, with a correction to the why: the house's page and Grandes Escolhas say the Falcoaria range is named for the royal falcon hunts once held on the land, not for the house's own falconry. Falcoaria Tinto is taught. The living family is never named.
casa-cadaval: answered. 1648 is the dukedom and the stud, not a founding, so founded stays empty; de and do Cadaval both appear; the red's grapes are the house's sheet; the Trincadeira is in others.

quinta-da-lagoalva: answered. The Alfrocheiro is taught; Dona Isabel Juliana is in others, a sparkling Grande Reserva Bruto among its wines. The why's horses and cork rest on one listing each by the author and are not in the prose.

companhia-das-lezirias: answered. The 1836 range is made red, white and sparkling; Tyto Alba is in others. The note's vines in the estuary's nature reserve rest on one account that places Catapereiro in the protected area, not settled.
